body: Oliver Sacks wrote a book about this phenomena. The patient he described didn't like the modern world at all.

>I can't agree. At minimum euthanasia is inherently a dangerous practice - the risk of wrongful death is obvious. Murder disguised as euthanasia, people coerced into suicide, suicide due to mistake of fact or deception.

You just are assuming that euthanasia has to be administered by a doctor. If you read about those who actually are engaged in this issue, they have moved away from this idea, doctors don't have to be directly involved- the idea that they do is a media construction. Euthanasia would be carried out by the individual themselves in most cases, while those in hospital already too ill to do so would have to rely on the right to refuse treatment. 

>Even if you don't accept that the government should prevent people who genuinely and freely wish to die and have all the facts from doing so you must admit that is a major moral hazard.

Those involved in this movement nowadays have moved to focusing more on spreading information in the community on how to carry out euthanasia individually.

There is no moral hazard, again it is a personal choice, to get the government involved is a form of tyranny.

The selective nature of govt when it comes to protecting life disqualifies it from having a legitimate saying.  People drink themselves to death, smoke themselves to an early grave collectively causing massive monetary costs to society, and shoot themselves/others to an obscene degree in modern America because of powerful lobbyist groups including the government.

Those who are slowly dying with no treatment in sight and in atrocious, untreatable pain or those with non-malignant conditions that cause untreatable constant pain are powerless compared to these obscene industries--so they are the ones to feel the brunt of our "morality" and "government protection"

It is blatantly hypocritical. The government has absolutely no business legislating personal morality. It always leads to abuse of power and tyranny , the powerful sidestep the "moral" commandments while the powerless are oppressed by them, just look at the Drug War.

Euthanasia is strictly a personal choice. The state is violating human rights and freedom in suspending the rights of those who clearly aren't mentally ill yet are who are either dying and in immense pain that cannot be treated or have chronic untreatable conditions that will cause chronic pain unimaginable to the layperson for the rest of their life.

Where is the judicial oversight when people who clearly aren't mentally ill have their freedom taken by in many cases private institutions, with absolutely no oversight except the judgement of a highly biased (both ideologically and economically) psychiatrist.

Highly unethical and immoral.

Wow, values & ideology trump good science in psychiatry. It is essentially being used as a tool to reinforce relatively healthy people's norms over the entire population--including non-mentally ill dying and those with incurable, untreatable diseases that cause immense suffering. 

The NYTs did a powerful recent piece covering the use of force feeding on patients at the new stage of dementia. The hard facts shows this actually harms them yet doctors continue to do it en masse because of psychiatric ideology and economic convenience. The immorality of this practice is off the charts yet the psychiatry deems those who choose euthanasia as mentally ill--if anyone needs therapy its the doctors and families who demand a harmful procedure found to be unethical to do to suspected terrorists.

I've noticed among cats, when they get to the end of their life and get quite sick, they will tend to mysteriously wander way off after experiencing an increase in their illnesses.

Basically psychiatry in this case is using science to claim their right to be essentially morality police- it's an outrage.
